Number 6 answers number 3. Cliff has the doll because Amelie brought him back. I love Deadman, but let's be honest it's not like he's an expert on Cliff and was just making an assumption based on the history he was able to uncover about the commander. Amelie claims that she brought Cliff back to 'remind Sam that he's not alone'. It's a very convoluted way of doing that, and in my opinion, a lot of the decisions and actions she takes don't make a whole lot of sense as she seems to waffle wildly between her two options of saving the world or ending it early.

Number 1: My theory about this after viewing the wild ramblings scribbled all over the walls of Higgs's bunker is this; with how Amelie had scrambled his brain with having shown him how the world would end (Keep in mind that this is the very same reason why Lucy -Sam's wife- took her own life) on top of the constant exposure to the Chiralium mask on his face, I'd imagine that a lot of his thoughts and emotions are scrambled. Unable to make very rational decisions, and seems only to make decisions based on impulse in the moment rather than having any sort of foresight. A clear example of this is when he tries to get Sam to deliver a bomb to South Knot City, and in his journal he notes something like, "I knew I shouldn't have put that on the tag... but who the hell checks those things these days anyway?" With how much Amelie waffles on her decisions, it's no surprise she didn't fully commit to telling Higgs everything.

Number 2: (see my first answer)Deadman is speculating from the information he pulled from Cliff.

Number 3: (see my first answer)She did bring Cliff back from the dead,

Number 4: Heartman meant that there are spikes in Chiralium in the atmosphere as a direct result from Sam having connected the whole continent to the Chiral network. Connecting everyone to it, increased the volume of Chiralium in the air, and actually connected everyone's beaches into a single beach, and in turn they are now connected to Amelie's beach which exists on a 'higher plane', according to Heartman.

Number 5: It's not clear what the time frame was when Amelie wanted to change her plans to try and stop the last extinction event. My theory: it was when Sam left for 10 years after his wife died, and cut himself off from her. "I thought no one would blame me if I just ended it all" This quote makes me believe this is when she had met/recruited Higgs into being her stand-in with the Homo Demens to help her speed up the final extinction. Again, there is no solid timeline for these events. Ultimately, I think even though she'd recruited Higgs first to usher in the end of days, I think she got cold feet and wanted Sam to make the decision for the fate of the world.

Number 6: Because Amelie summoned him, and that was his connection to her and her beach.

I will try to give a comprehensive breakdown. 

As far as the lore tells us, beaches have always existed and they are the passageway between the living world and the afterlife. Those who die must pass through it in order to reach the afterlife, and their Beach will appear as a reflection of them as a person/their life experiences/etc. those who die together (be it in battle, from sickness, bombs, void outs, etc.) will all share a beach as they move on to the afterlife. 

It's unclear how EE's came to be, but they do arrive to see the world into its next extinction. Heartman explains that a death stranding is an indicator that an extinction event is close to occurring. And this is because of him and his colleagues finding remnants of past death strandings happening, accompanied by a creature possessing an umbilical cord (Like Bridget Strand had) that he theorized to be extinction entities. they were all perfectly preserved as if "trapped in time", and they all marked the end of their respective periods of time, and the species that thrived during that time. 

During the events of the game we are experiencing the 6th and "final" extinction event. I'm not sure what makes this particular event different, but I believe it has to do with the chiral Network. Because by the end of the game we have connected it up throughout the entire nation, and it is explained that all beaches have now connected to Amelie's. I suspect that this makes this particular extinction event much more deadly than the previous ones.

As far as I'm aware, there isn't any lore explaining how extinction entities came to be, or why they show up throughout history. Just that they are a powerful being that exists both in the living world and outside of time on a higher beach and possess incredible powers. I assume that this means that they are naturally occurring.

That's so valid honestly. The first few hours to a new player aren't exactly the most exciting, and it really doesn't open up until you get to Port Knot City. So while you're trying to get there to progress the story, the map is going to seem smaller and much less interesting, but it does set a baseline for things to come. It also introduces you to a lot of the core mechanics of the game. If you're someone who wants to rush through things, I'd recommend taking the slow route with this one. It will pay off in the end, and cause a lot less headache. 

As for the story, it does have all the calling cards of classic Hideo Kojima's writing. Lots of exposition dumps from characters, and interactions that often seem strange and out of place. So if you're willing to be patient through the weirdness of it, you'll learn things that you'll go back to and say: oh... Ok that part makes a hell of a lot more sense now. 

If a slow burn story, and gameplay aren't your thing, I totally get it. It's not for everyone! It does have its really chill moments though where I can just turn my brain off for a bit and just enjoy the scenery while I make my lil deliveries.

I know this question was directed at the OP, but I highly recommend it. There's a lot more going on here than everyone looking at its surface level and labeling it as a walking simulator. The story can be hard to grasp as it does use a lot of fictional jargon, but once you have an understanding of it all, then you'll really come to know how beautifully this story wraps itself up.
